youtube.title: Cosmic Microwave Background: Why Were Pigeons Blamed?
youtube.description:
The cosmic microwave background, the oldest light in the universe, was first blamed on pigeons. Here is how the afterglow of the Big Bang was found by accident.

In 1964, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson at Bell Labs in New Jersey heard a faint hiss in their giant horn antenna, from every direction, day and night. Pigeons were nesting inside, so they cleaned out the droppings, but the hiss stayed. At Princeton, Robert Dicke heard the news and told his team, "Boys, we've been scooped." The discovery won the 1978 Nobel Prize in Physics.

Subscribe to Stickstory for one wild true story every day. What would you have blamed first? Tell me in the comments!

scenes.text: They blamed the Big Bang on pigeons.
scenes.visual: A grassy hill in New Jersey: the giant Holmdel horn antenna on its rail turntable, its long tapering horn rising to a dark square mouth; two grey pigeons strut and peck on the mouth's lip while faint gold hiss squiggles creep into the horn; the antenna gives a jolt on 'pigeons'.

scenes.text: In 1964, two Bell Labs scientists heard a hiss in their antenna,
scenes.visual: The Bell Labs receiver room: racks of equipment with dials and blinking lamps; on the near desk a pen chart recorder spits a long strip of graph paper that curls down to the floor, and from 'hiss' its red pen scribbles a jagged noise line; two scientists lean in behind the desk, frowning; cards '1964' and 'HISS'.

scenes.text: from every direction, day and night.
scenes.visual: The antenna in an open field swings slowly from side to side while gold hiss squiggles fly in from every edge of the sky; the sun sinks and on 'night' a moon rises; a red card 'EVERY DIRECTION'.

scenes.text: Pigeons were nesting inside, so they cleaned out the droppings.
scenes.visual: Inside the horn, looking down its corrugated throat: a twig nest with two pigeons on the floor, white droppings scattered all around; on 'cleaned' a broom sweeps in from the right and pushes the droppings away while the pigeons flap up and fly off.
Close on the chart recorder and its curling paper strip: the red pen still scribbles the same jagged noise across the scrolling graph paper; the two scientists stare; a red card 'STILL THERE'.

A Princeton physics office: a blackboard full of chalk equations; in the foreground a big black rotary phone rings and jumps on the desk, red ring marks around it, its cord hanging to the floor; the fez host, full figure in front of the desk, turns and points at it, surprised.

scenes.text: and Robert Dicke told his team, "Boys, we've been scooped."
scenes.visual: The same office: Robert Dicke, with glasses, turns from the phone on the desk to two colleagues, eyebrows up, gesturing; they gape with open mouths; chair backs in the foreground; a red card 'WE'VE BEEN SCOOPED' over the blackboard.

scenes.text: It was the afterglow of the Big Bang,
scenes.visual: Night sky over the hill: a huge oval all-sky map fills blob by blob with mottled red, gold and blue spots, shimmering; gold waves drift from it down into the horn antenna on the dark hill below; a red card 'AFTERGLOW'.

scenes.text: and it's still all around you.
scenes.visual: The antenna at night under the stars: the whole sky speckled with a faint shimmering gold glow, gold hiss squiggles drifting in from everywhere, the mouth of the horn glowing gold; a red card 'STILL HERE'.

scenes.text: Subscribe for a true story like this every day.
scenes.visual: Daylight on the hill: the fez host waves at the viewer in front of the horn antenna, a pigeon pecking on its lip, then points at the viewer with a big smile.
